title: AI-Native Is an Operating Model, Not a Tool
subtitle: A design leader who still builds — AI in production, and the maturity work underneath it

cv.label: Download CV (PDF)
cv.note: Tailored for the Director of User Experience role

bio.short: I lead design functions and I still build. The last year went into AI that runs in production — a support copilot, a fundraising system I built end to end, and prototypes engineering ships from. Before that, fifteen years raising UX maturity at Ninox, Datameer and Spreadshirt.
bio.long: The clearest thing to look at is the support copilot at Bibel TV. It drafts replies to viewer letters from the service handbook. Most of the design was deciding what it must not do. The system prompt carries an explicit restricted-topic list. It is manually operated and embedded in nothing, so a person has already read the letter before the model ever sees it and every send decision stays human. It went out fully optional, so it had to earn its place on the hard cases. The fundraising system I built alone, end to end: the analysis, the prompt architecture, the prototype, then the production skill. And the practice underneath both is agentic engineering — I prototype in real code against real APIs, and engineering ships from that code. Engineering at Bibel TV is an external agency, so that handoff crosses a company boundary and holds anyway. The longer thread is maturity. At Ninox I ran a collaborative self-assessment rather than imposing a model, established design as a function co-equal with product and engineering, and sat on the Senior Leadership Team with five reports including a design lead. I hired two, promoted two and let two go, covered Head of Product from July to October 2023, and hired the consultant who was then brought in to hold it. At Datameer I moved design from an execution function to a strategic partner and got executive support for research, including the screening method that reached analysts working inside banks. At Spreadshirt I was instrumental in the UX maturity transformation across a 200-plus-person matrix organization, harmonizing stakeholder relationships and driving UX team development across departments.

context.company: DocuWare — document digitization and workflow automation for enterprise, sold across many industries. Germering (Munich), New York, Sofia. Headcount not stated anywhere in the posting.
context.role: Director of User Experience, accountable for Research and Design, leading UX leaders across both. The posting rules out two shapes explicitly: 'a build-and-scale role, not a maintenance one… a maker and a leader who leads through the work — not a strategy-only or people-management-only role.'
context.emphasis: Lead with AI shipped into production and the trust decisions that made it shippable — the posting asks for a maker who leads through the work. Then UX maturity raised twice, each with a named method: a collaborative self-assessment at Ninox and a measured increase at Datameer. Spreadshirt is the transformation he was instrumental in rather than one he led, and it is never counted as a third. Then the people decisions at Ninox: five reports including a design lead, hired two, promoted two, let two go, interim Head of Product July to October 2023, and the successor hire.
